mainTopic: Stories of the חכמים: אליהו's rebuke, the size and beauty of the חכמים, and the friendship and loss of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
overview: This amud is all אגדה, stories rather than legal debate. It opens with אליהו הנביא rebuking רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי for handing Jews over to the Roman government, telling him to run away as his father did. Next the גמרא describes how large רבי ישמעאל and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון were, and how they answered a Roman noblewoman who mocked them. The גמרא explains that they answered her only to protect their children's good name. It then turns to רבי יוחנן's great beauty, and to why he sat by the מקוה without fearing the עין הרע: he came from יוסף. Then comes the famous story of how רבי יוחנן brought ריש לקיש, a bandit, to Torah and made him a great scholar. After a sharp exchange in the בית מדרש, רבי יוחנן was hurt, ריש לקיש fell ill and died, and רבי יוחנן mourned him so deeply that no one could replace him, until he too died.

steps.title: אליהו challenges רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: A government job of catching criminals comes to רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי. אליהו meets him and asks how long he will keep handing Jews over to be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A case like this came to him. אליהו met him and said to him: Until when will you hand over the nation of our God to be killed?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי now has the same kind of government job, and אליהו הנביא confronts him about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'a case like this' links him to the earlier story, where a fellow חכם was appointed to catch thieves for the government. אליהו's question is not really a request for information. It is a sharp criticism: handing Jews to the government can lead to their execution.

keyTerms.meaning: He met him, came across him
Hands over, informs on someone to the authorities

phrases.english: a case like this came into his hands.
Elijah met him,
and said to him: Until when
will you hand over the nation of our God
to be killed?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּגַע בֵּיהּ אֵלִיָּהוּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַד מָתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier story about חכמים who worked for the Roman government.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's choice to serve the government by handing over Jews
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Handing Jews to a foreign government can get them executed, so a חכם should not take part in it.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל says he has no choice
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל defends himself: the king ordered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What can I do? It is the king's order!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי answers אליהו by saying he is being forced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His defense is that he is not acting by choice. Refusing a royal order is dangerous, so in his view he has no option.

phrases.english: He said to him: What can I do?
It is the king's order!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אליהו's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Claim of being forced by outside authority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He is guilty of willingly handing over Jews.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is only obeying a royal order he cannot refuse.

steps.title: אליהו says: run away like your father did
steps.stepSummary: אליהו rejects the excuse. His father fled to אסיא, so he can flee to לודקיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Your father ran away to אסיא; you run away to לודקיא.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו pushes back on the excuse by showing that there was a way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim 'I have no choice' falls apart because his own father, רבי יוסי, escaped a similar situation by leaving. So he too could run away rather than serve the government.
steps.whatToRemember: אליהו did not accept 'the king made me do it' as an excuse. If running away is possible, a person should run rather than hand Jews over.

phrases.english: He said to him: Your father ran away to Asia,
you run away to Laodicea.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבוּךְ עֲרַק לְאַסְיָא, אַתְּ עֲרוֹק לְלוּדְקִיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the excuse given in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole claim of being forced
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There was an escape, since his father had already shown that running away is possible.

steps.title: The two חכמים were so large that oxen fit between them
steps.stepSummary: When רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון stood together, a pair of oxen could walk between them without touching them.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון met each other, a pair of oxen could pass between them without touching them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new short story about these same two חכמים, describing how large their bellies were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their bellies were so big that when the two stood face to face, there was space under them for a team of oxen to pass. This description sets up the noblewoman's mocking remark that comes next.

phrases.english: When they would meet
Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei,
and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon,
each other,
a pair of oxen could enter between them
and it would not touch them.
phrases.notes: He means the oxen fit under their bellies, which stuck out so far.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹ מִקַּלְעִי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the government story to a new story about the same חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two חכמים were extremely large.

steps.title: A noblewoman claims their children are not theirs
steps.stepSummary: A Roman noblewoman says that, because of their size, their children cannot really be theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain noblewoman said to them: Your children are not yours.
steps.whatsHappening: A Roman noblewoman mocks the two חכמים and implies they could not have fathered their own children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her argument is that men this large could not be with their wives. That would mean their wives had children from other men, which is an insult to their families.

phrases.english: A certain noblewoman said to them:
Your children are not yours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לְהוּ הָהִיא מַטְרוֹנִיתָא: בְּנֵיכֶם אֵינָם שֶׁלָּכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the description of their size in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the חכמים truly fathered their children
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their size would make relations with their wives impossible.

steps.title: They answer that their wives are even larger
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply that their wives' bellies are bigger than their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to her: Theirs is bigger than ours.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give a short, sharp reply to the noblewoman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Theirs' means their wives' bellies. The answer is witty more than logical: if size were the problem, their wives are even bigger.

phrases.english: They said to her: Theirs is bigger than ours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the noblewoman's insult.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Their size proves the children are not theirs.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their wives are even larger, which brushes the insult aside.

steps.title: She says: all the more so
steps.stepSummary: The noblewoman turns their answer against them: if the wives are larger too, it is even less possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The noblewoman uses their own answer to make her point stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both husband and wife are very large, being together is even harder. So their answer only seems to strengthen her claim.

phrases.english: All the more so!
phrases.notes: The noblewoman is the one saying this. The גמרא doesn't spell out who speaks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 6 as a counterattack.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer 'theirs is bigger than ours'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bigger wives make it even less possible, not more.

steps.title: Another version: a פסוק, 'as the man, so is his strength'
steps.stepSummary: According to some, the חכמים answered her by quoting a פסוק: 'For as the man is, so is his strength.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is what they said to her: 'For as the man is, so is his strength.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of what the חכמים answered the noblewoman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a פסוק, they hint that a man's body is proportioned to his size. So a large man is not prevented from fathering children.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say, another version

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a separate story. It is another version of the same answer the חכמים gave the noblewoman.

phrases.english: There are those who say this is what they said to her:
"For as the man is, so is his strength."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the חכמים' answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Their size makes fathering children impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: A man's strength matches his size, so there is no problem.

steps.title: A third version: love compresses the flesh
steps.stepSummary: According to others, the חכמים answered: 'Love compresses the flesh.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is what they said to her: 'Love compresses the flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third version of the חכמים' answer to the noblewoman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the answer is that love between husband and wife overcomes physical obstacles. Size does not stand in the way where there is love.
steps.whatToRemember: The noblewoman's insult gets three versions of an answer: their wives are larger, a man's strength matches his size, and love overcomes the body.

phrases.english: There are those who say this is what they said to her:
"Love compresses the flesh."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative version of the answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Their size makes being together impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: Love makes the physical obstacle disappear.

steps.title: Why answer a foolish question at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the חכמים for answering the noblewoman, since a פסוק in משלי says not to answer a fool.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they need to answer her? It is written: 'Answer not a fool according to his folly'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and asks why the חכמים answered her rude question at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The noblewoman's question was insulting and foolish. The פסוק in משלי tells us not to answer a fool like that. So the חכמים seem to have gone against this advice.

phrases.english: And why did they need to answer her?
But it is written:
"Answer not a fool according to his folly"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the behavior of the חכמים in the exchange from steps 5-9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that the חכמים answered the noblewoman's question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says not to answer a fool, and her question was foolish, so they should have stayed silent.

steps.title: They answered to protect their children's good name
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answered so that no one would spread doubts about whether their children were really theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: So as not to spread a bad name about their children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: they replied so that rumors would not spread about their children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually it is better not to answer a fool. But here, staying silent could make people think her claim was true, and their children would be suspected. Protecting the children's good name was more important.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule not to answer a fool has an exception: you should answer when silence would harm other people's reputation.

phrases.english: So as not to spread a bad name about their children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special reason overrides the general advice of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים should have ignored her, as the פסוק advises.
steps.terutzMaskana: Silence would have left a stain on their children's lineage, so answering was proper.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן on the size of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports the very large body size of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The organ of רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי was like a jug holding nine קבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the topic of how large these חכמים were, starting with a report from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds detail to the story of the noblewoman. It shows that these חכמים really were unusually large. The measure is given with a jug of a certain size.

keyTerms.meaning: his body part (here, his private organ)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The organ of Rabbi Yishmael [son of Rabbi Yosei]
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets.

phrases.english: was like a jug holding nine kav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵיבְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the noblewoman story to reports about the physical size of the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי was extremely large.

steps.title: רב פפא on the size of רבי יוחנן, and רב פפא himself
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reports רבי יוחנן's size, with two versions, and the גמרא notes that רב פפא himself had a huge belly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The organ of רבי יוחנן was like a jug of five קבין, and some say three קבין. רב פפא himself had a belly like the baskets of הרפניא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a second report, this time about רבי יוחנן. The גמרא then adds a side remark about רב פפא's own size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of רב פפא's report: five קבין or three. The last line is the גמרא's own comment. It shows that רב פפא was also a very large man.

keyTerms.meaning: of הרפניא, a town in בבל

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The organ of Rabbi Yoḥanan
was like a jug holding five kav,
and some say, holding three kav.
Rav Pappa himself had a belly
like the baskets of Harpanya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֵיבְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another report in the same style as step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן and רב פפא were also very large.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's beauty
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says he is the last of Jerusalem's beautiful people, and the גמרא gives a picture to show his beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: I am the only one left of the beautiful people of Jerusalem. Whoever wants to see something like רבי יוחנן's beauty should take a shiny new silver cup, fill it with red pomegranate seeds, put a ring of red roses around its rim, and place it between sunlight and shade. That glow is a little like רבי יוחנן's beauty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן says he is the last beautiful person from Jerusalem. Then the גמרא describes a scene that helps us picture how he looked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic moves from size to beauty. The picture uses a shining silver cup, red seeds, and red roses, half in sun and half in shade. The glow from all this is only 'like' his beauty, not the full thing.

keyTerms.meaning: I was left over, I remain
something like, a small taste of

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
I alone remain of the beautiful people of Jerusalem.
Whoever wants
phrases.notes: From here on it's the גמרא speaking, not רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: to see the beauty of Rabbi Yoḥanan
should bring a silver cup fresh from the silversmith,
and fill it with seeds of a red pomegranate,

phrases.aramaic: וְנַהְדַּר לֵיהּ כְּלִילָא דְּוַורְדָּא סוּמָּקָא לְפוּמֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: and put a ring of red roses around its rim,
and set it between the sunlight and the shade.
That glow
phrases.notes: Some versions say הָהוּא ('that') and some say הָנְהוּ ('those'). Either way, it's the shining glow just described.

phrases.english: is a small taste of Rabbi Yoḥanan's beauty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֲנָא אִשְׁתַּיַּירִי מִשַּׁפִּירֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with רבי יוחנן's body, moving from his size to his beauty.

steps.title: Why is רבי יוחנן missing from the list of beautiful people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a list of beautiful people that reaches back to אדם הראשון, and רבי יוחנן is not on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But the Master said: רב כהנא's beauty is like רבי אבהו's; רבי אבהו's beauty is like יעקב אבינו's; יעקב אבינו's beauty is like אדם הראשון's. And רבי יוחנן is not counted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוחנן was really so beautiful. It points to a known list of the most beautiful people, which leaves him out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list goes step by step: רב כהנא, then רבי אבהו, then יעקב אבינו, then אדם הראשון. If רבי יוחנן was so beautiful, he should be on it. Leaving him out suggests he was not that beautiful.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't the Master say:
The beauty of Rav Kahana
is like the beauty of Rabbi Abbahu;
the beauty of Rabbi Abbahu
is like the beauty of Jacob our father;
the beauty of Jacob our father
is like the beauty of Adam the first man!

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא קָא חָשֵׁיב לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: Yet Rabbi Yoḥanan is not counted on the list!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of step 14 about רבי יוחנן's beauty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן was extremely beautiful.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known list of the most beautiful people leaves him out, which suggests he was not among them.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן had no beard
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן is different because he had no beard, so he was left off the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן is different, because he did not have the glory of the face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן was left off the list because he had no beard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list counts full beauty, which includes a beard. רבי יוחנן was very beautiful, but he had no beard. So he was not counted, even though step 14 is still true.

keyTerms.meaning: glory of the face, meaning a beard

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן was truly beautiful. He is missing from the list only because he had no beard, which the list counted as part of full beauty.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan is different,
because he did not have the glory of the face.
phrases.notes: 'Glory of the face' means a beard; רבי יוחנן had none.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving רבי יוחנן off the list shows he was not truly beautiful.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was very beautiful but lacked a beard, so he was not counted on the list.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן sits by the gates of the מקוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן sat by the gates of the מקוה so women coming from טבילה would see him and have sons who were beautiful and learned like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן would go and sit at the gates of the immersion place. He said: When Jewish women come up from the מצוה immersion, let them meet me, so that they will have sons as beautiful as me and as learned in Torah as me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the topic of רבי יוחנן's beauty with a story about what he did with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן wanted the women to see him right after טבילת מצוה. He hoped this would lead to children who were beautiful and learned in Torah like him. This sets up the next question about the עין הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: The gates or entrance of the place of immersion (the מקוה)
An immersion done for a מצוה, here a woman's טבילה
Let them meet me (see me first)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan would go
and sit at the gates of the immersion place.
He said: When Jewish women come up
from the מצוה immersion, let them meet me,
so that they will have
sons as beautiful as me,
learned in Torah like me.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה אָזֵיל וְיָתֵיב אַשַּׁעֲרֵי טְבִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of רבי יוחנן's beauty from steps 14-16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן sat by the מקוה so women would see him and have beautiful, learned children.

steps.title: Aren't you afraid of the evil eye?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask רבי יוחנן whether he worries that showing himself like this will bring the עין הרע on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said to him: Isn't the master afraid of the evil eye?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge what רבי יוחנן is doing. This question sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Showing off great beauty in public could invite the עין הרע. The question is worded as a question, but it works as a challenge to his behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: The master (a respectful way to say 'you')

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to him:
Isn't the master afraid of the evil eye?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the behavior described in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's practice of sitting in public by the מקוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Showing himself in public should put him in danger of the עין הרע.

steps.title: יוסף's descendants are above the evil eye
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that he comes from יוסף, and the עין הרע has no power over יוסף's descendants. רבי אבהו reads the פסוק 'עלי עין' as 'עולי עין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I come from the seed of יוסף, over whom the evil eye has no control. As it is written: 'יוסף is a fruitful son, a fruitful son by a spring (עלי עין).' And רבי אבהו said: Do not read 'עלי עין' but 'עולי עין', those who rise above the eye.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge: the עין הרע cannot harm him because he is from זרעו של יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a פסוק from יעקב's ברכה to יוסף. רבי אבהו reads the words 'עלי עין' (by a spring) as 'עולי עין' (rising above the eye). So יוסף's family is above the power of the עין הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read (the word this way, but read it another way)
Those who rise above the eye

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֲנָא מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף קָאָתֵינָא,
phrases.english: He said to them: I come from the seed of Yosef,
over whom the evil eye has no control.
As it is written: "Yosef is a fruitful son,
a fruitful son by a spring (alei ayin)"
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:22. The word עין can mean a spring or an eye.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abahu said:
Do not read "alei ayin" (by a spring)
but "olei ayin" (those who rise above the eye).
phrases.notes: He means יוסף's family rises above the evil eye, so it can't hurt them.

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' doesn't mean the פסוק is wrong. It's a way of reading an extra lesson into the words alongside their plain meaning.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the עין הרע challenge from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exemption based on family line, supported by a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן should be in danger of the עין הרע like anyone else.
steps.terutzMaskana: As a descendant of יוסף, he is immune to the עין הרע.

steps.title: A second source: like fish hidden in the sea
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא learns the same idea from 'וידגו לרב': like fish covered by water, יוסף's descendants are not reached by the עין הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said it is learned from here: 'And may they multiply like fish in the midst of the land.' Just as fish in the sea are covered by water and the eye has no control over them, so too the eye has no control over יוסף's descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different פסוק as a source for the same idea, that the עין הרע can't harm Yosef's family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וידגו' comes from 'דג', fish. Fish are hidden under water, so no eye rests on them. The ברכה compares יוסף's family to fish, so they are also protected from the עין הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: And may they multiply (connected to דָּג, fish)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אֲמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said: it is learned from here:
"And may they multiply like fish in the midst of the land."
phrases.notes: בראשית 48:16, יעקב's ברכה to יוסף's sons.

phrases.english: Just as fish in the sea,
water covers them
and the eye has no control over them,
so too, the descendants of Yosef,
the eye has no control over them.

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources teach that the עין הרע has no power over זרעו של יוסף: 'עולי עין' (רבי אבהו) and 'וידגו', like fish (רבי יוסי בר חנינא).
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אֲמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second פסוק for the idea in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the עין הרע has no power over Yosef's descendants
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 48:16, 'וידגו לרב': fish hidden under water are not seen.

steps.title: ריש לקיש jumps into the Jordan after רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש saw רבי יוחנן bathing in the ירדן and jumped in after him. רבי יוחנן said his strength belongs to Torah, and ריש לקיש said רבי יוחנן's beauty belongs to women.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day רבי יוחנן was bathing in the Jordan. ריש לקיש saw him and jumped into the Jordan after him. רבי יוחנן said to him: Your strength should be for Torah. ריש לקיש said to him: Your beauty should be for women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story connected to רבי יוחנן's beauty, telling how he first met ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's huge jump shows great physical strength, and רבי יוחנן says that strength should go to Torah. ריש לקיש answers that רבי יוחנן's beauty fits a woman. This sets up the deal in the next step.

phrases.english: One day was bathing
Rabbi Yochanan, in the Jordan.
Reish Lakish saw him
and jumped into the Jordan after him.
He said to him: Your strength, for Torah.
phrases.notes: Here רבי יוחנן is speaking: such strength should be used for learning Torah.

phrases.english: He said to him: Your beauty, for women.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד הֲוָה קָא סָחֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּיַרְדְּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story still tied to the theme of רבי יוחנן's beauty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן tells ריש לקיש that his strength belongs to Torah.

steps.title: ריש לקיש accepts and loses his strength
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן offers his more beautiful sister if ריש לקיש returns to Torah. ריש לקיש accepts, and then cannot jump back for his clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: If you return to the right path, I will give you my sister, who is more beautiful than me. He accepted it upon himself. He wanted to go back to bring his clothes, but he was not able to go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: רבי יוחנן makes an offer, ריש לקיש accepts, and right away he finds he can't jump back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offer answers ריש לקיש's remark about beauty: his sister is even more beautiful. Once ריש לקיש takes Torah upon himself, his great jumping strength is gone. The same strength that impressed רבי יוחנן is now gone.

keyTerms.meaning: You turn back, change your ways

phrases.english: He said to him: If you turn back (to Torah),
I will give you my sister,
who is more beautiful than me.
He accepted it upon himself.
He wanted to go back to bring his clothes
but he was not able to go back.

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's strength led רבי יוחנן to say it belonged to Torah, and once ריש לקיש accepted Torah, that strength was gone.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָדְרַתְּ בָּךְ יָהֵיבְנָא לָךְ אֲחוֹתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ריש לקיש story from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש accepts Torah for the promise of רבי יוחנן's sister and immediately loses his physical strength.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן turns ריש לקיש into a great scholar
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches ריש לקיש מקרא and משנה until he becomes a great man.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught him Bible, taught him משנה, and made him into a great man.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. ריש לקיש has come back to Torah, and רבי יוחנן teaches him until he becomes a great scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line closes the deal from step 22. ריש לקיש returned to Torah, and רבי יוחנן built him up from the basics of תנ"ך and משנה into a major תלמיד חכם. That background matters for the argument that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught him מקרא (the written Torah)
A great man, meaning a major Torah scholar

phrases.english: He taught him Bible and taught him Mishna,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יוחנן, and "him" is ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: and made him into a great man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story. ריש לקיש accepted the offer, and now רבי יוחנן teaches him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש became a great Torah scholar through רבי יוחנן's teaching.

steps.title: A study hall discussion about when weapons can become impure
steps.stepSummary: The בית מדרש discusses a source stating that metal weapons and blades receive טומאה once their manufacture is complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day they were arguing in the study hall: the sword, the knife, the dagger, the spear, the hand sickle and the harvest sickle, from when can they become טמא? From the time their manufacture is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the scene for the argument. It brings a rule that weapons and blades can become טמא once they are finished being made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A metal vessel can only receive טומאה once it is a completed vessel. This source gives the rule, "once their work is finished," but leaves open exactly when that is. That open question is what the next step asks.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד הֲווֹ מִפַּלְגִי בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא:
phrases.english: One day they were arguing in the study hall:
The sword, the knife, the dagger, and the spear,
and a hand sickle and a harvest sickle,
from when can they become impure?
From the time their manufacture is finished.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד הֲווֹ מִפַּלְגִי בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new scene in the story. Now the two are learning together as scholars.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Metal weapons and blades receive טומאה from when their manufacture is complete.

steps.title: When exactly is their manufacture finished?
steps.stepSummary: The בית מדרש asks at what point the manufacture of these blades counts as finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from when is their manufacture finished?
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars ask exactly when a blade counts as "finished." This sets up the disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source in step 24 gave a general rule, "once finished." Here the scholars want the exact stage in making the blade.

phrases.english: And from when is their manufacture finished?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a clear definition of the term "finished" used in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which stage of the metalworking process counts as the completion of the vessel.

steps.title: Furnace or water: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the blade is finished once it is fired in the furnace. ריש לקיש says it is finished only once it is polished in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: once he fires them in the furnace. ריש לקיש said: once he polishes them in water.
steps.whatsHappening: Two answers are given. רבי יוחנן says the blade is finished after the furnace. ריש לקיש says it is finished later, after it is polished in water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's view moves the point of completion one stage later, so the blade cannot become טמא until it has been dipped and polished. His view shows inside knowledge of how weapons are made, and that sets up the next remark.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
From when one fires them in the furnace.
Reish Lakish said:
From when one polishes them in water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 with two opposing views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: completion is at firing in the furnace. ריש לקיש: completion is at polishing in water.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's remark: a bandit knows his trade
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן remarks that ריש לקיש knows about weapons because of his past as a bandit.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A bandit knows about his banditry.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן responds to ריש לקיש's view with a sharp remark. He says ריש לקיש knows weapons so well because he used to be a bandit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a legal proof. It is a personal comment pointing to ריש לקיש's past. That turns a הלכה discussion into a personal hurt.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A bandit knows about his banditry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A personal reaction to ריש לקיש's opinion in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן links ריש לקיש's expertise to his past as a bandit.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: What did you do for me?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers back: as a bandit he was called "chief," and here too he is called "chief," so what did רבי יוחנן gain him?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What good did you do me? There they called me "chief," and here they call me "chief"!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש is hurt and pushes back. He says he had a leading title among the bandits and has one in Torah too, so bringing him to Torah did not raise his status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש challenges what רבי יוחנן did for him, measured by honor and title. If he was a leader before and is a leader now, what changed? The next step answers that.

keyTerms.meaning: There (among the bandits) / here (in the study hall)

phrases.english: He said to him: And what benefit did you give me?
There they called me "Rabbi,"
phrases.notes: Here רַבִּי means "chief" or "master." Among the bandits he was their leader.

phrases.english: here they call me "Rabbi"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the hurtful remark of step 27 with a counter-challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The value of רבי יוחנן bringing ריש לקיש to Torah.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His title and status are the same as before, so the change gave him nothing new.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: I brought you under the wings of the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the real benefit was bringing ריש לקיש close to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did you good, because I brought you close under the wings of the שכינה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש's complaint. The gain was not a title. It was coming close to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש measured the change by status. רבי יוחנן says it should be measured by closeness to the שכינה, which a bandit chief never had.

keyTerms.meaning: Under the wings of the Divine Presence

phrases.english: He said to him: I benefited you,
for I brought you close, under the wings of the Divine Presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהֲנַאי לָךְ דַּאֲקָרְבִינָּךְ תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge from step 28.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The benefit should be measured by honor and title.
steps.terutzMaskana: The true benefit is closeness to the שכינה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is hurt, and ריש לקיש falls ill
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן was offended, and as a result ריש לקיש became sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן was hurt, and ריש לקיש became ill.
steps.whatsHappening: The argument leaves רבי יוחנן deeply hurt. As a result, ריש לקיש becomes sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא links the two events directly. The pain of a great צדיק had a real effect on ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He was hurt or upset (his mind grew weak)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan was offended,
and Reish Lakish fell ill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what the exchange in steps 27 to 29 led to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן's hurt led to ריש לקיש's illness.

steps.title: His sister pleads, and רבי יוחנן answers with a verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's sister begs him to pray for her husband, for her children's sake and for her own. He answers each plea with part of a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: His sister came crying. She said: Do it for my children! He said: "Leave your orphans, I will keep them alive." She said: Do it for my widowhood! He said: "And let your widows trust in Me."
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש's wife, who is רבי יוחנן's sister, comes crying and asks him to help her husband. He answers both of her pleas with a פסוק saying ה׳ will care for orphans and widows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She makes two pleas: the children need a father, and she does not want to become a widow. He answers each with the matching half of the same פסוק, which means ה׳ will take care of them. He does not agree to help ריש לקיש recover.

phrases.english: His sister came crying.
phrases.notes: This is the sister from step 22, who is now ריש לקיש's wife.

phrases.english: She said to him: Do it for the sake of my children!
He said to her: "Leave your fatherless children, I will rear them."
Do it for the sake of my widowhood!
He said to her: "And let your widows trust in Me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to ריש לקיש's illness from step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן answers his sister's pleas with ירמיהו 49:11 and does not act to save ריש לקיש.

steps.title: ריש לקיש dies, and רבי יוחנן grieves deeply
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש dies, and רבי יוחנן is in great pain over losing him.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש passed away, and רבי יוחנן was very pained after him.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש passes away. רבי יוחנן is overwhelmed with grief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story turns. The same רבי יוחנן who was hurt by ריש לקיש now cannot bear losing him, which shows how deep their bond was.

phrases.aramaic: נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish died,
phrases.notes: This is ריש לקיש's full name.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲוָה קָא מִצְטַעַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בָּתְרֵיהּ טוּבָא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yoḥanan was very pained over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The result of the illness from steps 30 and 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש died, and רבי יוחנן grieved greatly.

steps.title: Who will comfort רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask who should go to settle רבי יוחנן's mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said: Who should go to settle his mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן are worried about רבי יוחנן and ask who can go comfort him. This sets up their choice in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His grief is so strong that the רבנן look for a specific person who can ease it. That suggests the comforter must in some way fill ריש לקיש's place.

keyTerms.meaning: To settle his mind, to comfort him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ רַבָּנַן: מַאן לֵיזִיל לְיַתֹּבֵיהּ לְדַעְתֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: The Rabbis said: Who will go to settle his mind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי יוחנן's grief from step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is fit to comfort רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: They choose רבי אלעזר בן פדת for his sharp teachings
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן decide to send רבי אלעזר בן פדת, because his teachings are sharp.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רבי אלעזר בן פדת go, because his teachings are sharp.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן choose רבי אלעזר בן פדת to comfort רבי יוחנן. Their reason is that he is a sharp scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They think a sharp learning partner can replace the one רבי יוחנן lost. The story will continue to show whether this works.

phrases.english: Let Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat go,
for his teachings are sharp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר בן פדת, chosen because his teachings are sharp.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר supports every statement with a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן פדת sits with רבי יוחנן and backs up everything he says with a supporting ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and sat in front of רבי יוחנן. For every teaching רבי יוחנן said, he answered: there is a ברייתא that supports you.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the comforter the רבנן chose now goes to learn with רבי יוחנן. His method is to bring a proof for everything רבי יוחנן says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 34, רבי אלעזר בן פדת was chosen because his teachings are sharp. Here we see how he used that sharpness: he found sources that agreed with רבי יוחנן. This sets up רבי יוחנן's reaction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter, a teaching or statement
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: He went and sat before him.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אלעזר בן פדת, the one the רבנן chose in the last step.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מִילְּתָא דַּהֲוָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Every matter that רבי יוחנן would say,
he would say to him: there is a ברייתא that supports you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the decision from step 34: the chosen comforter goes to רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר בן פדת supported each of רבי יוחנן's statements with a ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן explains why agreement cannot replace ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says ריש לקיש's twenty-four challenges, and his own twenty-four answers, made the learning grow. A supporting source only tells him what he already knows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Are you like בר לקישא? When I said something, בר לקישא would ask me twenty-four questions. I would give twenty-four answers, and the teaching became clear and wide on its own. You just tell me a ברייתא supports me. Don't I already know that what I say is right?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן turns down the comfort he was offered. He explains what made ריש לקיש special as a learning partner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן פדת's proofs only confirm that רבי יוחנן is right. ריש לקיש's attacks forced him to defend and sharpen every idea, and that made the learning deeper. So agreement, however sharp, cannot fill the gap that ריש לקיש left.

keyTerms.meaning: Questions or challenges against a statement
The teaching becomes broadened and clarified
Is it that...? (a question that expects "no")

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן valued the חברותא who challenged him more than the one who agreed with him. Real growth in learning comes from questions and answers.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying a supporting ברייתא is worthless in general. He is saying it adds nothing new for him, because he already knows his statement is correct.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic Talmudic picture of a true חברותא: someone who pushes back. The back-and-forth is what makes the learning grow.

phrases.english: He said: Are you like the son of Lakish?!

phrases.aramaic: בַּר לְקִישָׁא, כִּי הֲוָה אָמֵינָא מִילְּתָא,
phrases.english: The son of Lakish, when I would say a matter,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מַקְשֵׁי לִי עֶשְׂרִין וְאַרְבַּע קוּשְׁיָיתָא,
phrases.english: would raise against me twenty-four difficulties,
and I would answer him with twenty-four answers,
and by itself the teaching would become broadened.
And you say: "There is a ברייתא that supports you"?
Do I not know that what I say is good?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers and rejects רבי אלעזר בן פדת's way of learning from step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being challenged makes the learning grow. Being agreed with does not, so nobody can replace ריש לקיש.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן cries out for ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן wanders, tears his clothes, weeps, and calls out for ריש לקיש again and again.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would walk around tearing his clothes and crying, saying: "Where are you, בר לקישא? Where are you, בר לקישא?"
steps.whatsHappening: The attempt to comfort him has failed. The גמרא now describes how deep רבי יוחנן's mourning was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing clothes and weeping are signs of mourning. The repeated cry "where are you" shows that he cannot accept the loss. This leads into the ending in the next step.

phrases.english: He would go around and tear his clothes
and weep and say:
"Where are you, son of Lakish,
where are you, son of Lakish!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After turning down the comfort in step 36, רבי יוחנן falls into deep mourning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן could not be comforted and mourned openly for ריש לקיש.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן loses his mind and dies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן screams until his mind leaves him. The רבנן pray for mercy for him, and he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: He kept screaming until his mind left him. The רבנן asked for mercy for him, and he died.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the story. רבי יוחנן's grief overwhelms him, and after the רבנן pray for him, he passes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story that began with a sharp word between the two friends ends with both of them gone. רבי יוחנן's grief went so far that he lost his sanity. The רבנן's prayer for mercy is followed directly by his death.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind left him; he lost his sanity
They asked for mercy, they prayed

steps.whatToRemember: The story ends in tragedy. A sharp exchange left רבי יוחנן hurt, ריש לקיש fell ill and died, and רבי יוחנן could not live without his חברותא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ending closes the whole story of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. It shows the cost of hurting someone with words, and how deep a true learning partnership can be.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲוָה קָא צָוַח עַד דְּשָׁף דַּעְתֵּיהּ מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: And he would scream until his mind was taken from him.
The רבנן asked for mercy for him
and his soul came to rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲוָה קָא צָוַח עַד דְּשָׁף דַּעְתֵּיהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the mourning from step 37 and ends the story with רבי יוחנן's death.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's grief over ריש לקיש was so great that he lost his mind. After the רבנן prayed for mercy for him, he died.
